mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Y-o-y GDPC1 growth accelerates by > 2pp but SPX 60-day forward returns are negative > 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When the ISM manufacturing index (proxied by INDPRO) falls below 45, indicating a contraction in manufacturing activity, it predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the economy heads towards recession.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 45 but SPX 20-day forward returns are positive > 60% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5pp over 3 months signals a rapidly weakening labor market, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending slows.
failure_condition: UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 3 months but SPX 60-day forward returns are positive > 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3%, it signals an overheating economy that will likely prompt the Fed to raise interest rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as discount rates rise.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 3% but SPX 20-day forward returns are positive > 60% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) rise by more than 10% year-over-year, it signals strong consumer demand that will boost economic growth and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Y-o-y HOUST growth > 10% but SPX 60-day forward returns are negative > 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by less than 100,000 jobs per month for 3 consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 3-month PAYEMS avg < 100,000 but SPX 20-day forward returns are positive > 60% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When real retail sales (RSAFS) fall by more than 5% year-over-year, and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 6%, it signals a severe demand slump that predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS y-o-y < -5% and UNRATE > 6% but SPX 60-day forward returns are positive > 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and rising, and the ISM manufacturing index (INDPRO) is below 50, it signals a monetary tightening cycle that will slow economic growth and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 5% and rising, INDPRO < 50, but SPX 20-day forward returns are positive > 60% of the time.
